text:
Logan Cooley scored three goals for the Mammoth, and the one that mattered most came with one second left in the third period. Pittsburgh's Ben Kindel had just put the Penguins up 3-2 at 19:35, with the building ready to celebrate, when Cooley tipped one in at 19:59 to tie it. Mikhail Sergachev then won it for UTA at 3:27 of overtime. Cooley, the third overall pick in 2022 who arrived after a 60-point season at Minnesota, had also scored the first two goals of the night.

The result matched the play, and then some. By our numbers, which weigh each shot by how likely it was to score (expected goals), UTA created 4.79 to PIT's 2.79. Replaying every shot many times, UTA wins this game 78% of the time. Shots on goal were even at 34, but UTA led in hits (25 to 7) and won more faceoffs (32 of 57). Pittsburgh was level through the first period and hung close, and Rickard Rakell's short-handed goal in the third tied it at 2-2. UTA pulled away late: its expected goals climbed to 1.52 to 0.67 in the third and 1.33 to 0.36 in overtime. Cooley also had a 25% chance in overtime go wide before Sergachev finished it.

Arturs Silovs stopped 30 of 34 for PIT and finished 0.79 goals better than expected, so the Penguins were never out of it. Sebastian Cossa made 31 saves for UTA. The two teams had already played on Oct. 19, a 5-4 UTA win, so the Mammoth now hold both meetings this season.
